questions.text: Why does linking fail with undefined reference to pthread_create only on the oldest Linux image?
questions.answer: The oldest Linux image uses glibc 2.31, where POSIX thread functions like pthread_create reside in a separate libpthread library that must be explicitly linked, whereas newer images use glibc 2.34 or later where these functions are integrated into the main C library.

questions.text: Linking test binaries runs out of memory on CI. How can the number of simultaneous links be limited?
questions.answer: Limit the number of simultaneous links by configuring a Ninja job pool that allows only two link jobs to run at a time, while keeping full parallelism for compile jobs. This is achieved by setting the global property JOB_POOLS to define a link_pool with a limit of 2 and assigning CMAKE_JOB_POOL_LINK to that pool.

questions.text: CMake cannot find the OpenSSL that Homebrew installed on a Mac. What should the configure step pass?
questions.answer: The configure step should pass the Homebrew prefix for the OpenSSL formula to CMake using the CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH variable, for example: cmake --preset release -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)".

questions.text: How are aarch64 tests run on x86_64 CI runners?
questions.answer: Orbit sets CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR to qemu-aarch64 -L /opt/sysroots/aarch64, allowing ctest to execute each aarch64 test binary through QEMU user-mode emulation on the x86_64 runner.

questions.text: What happens to a build when the remote cache cannot be reached?
questions.answer: When the remote cache is unreachable, Bazel treats the failed lookup as a cache miss, prints a warning, and runs the action locally, which makes the build slower but does not cause it to fail.

questions.text: Benchmarks built with Ninja are unexpectedly slow and no build type was chosen. Why?
questions.answer: Leaving CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE empty with a single-configuration generator like Ninja produces a build with no optimization flags, which is a common cause of unexpectedly slow benchmark numbers.
